title: Bonds to Increase Safety, Security; Repair, Construct Schools; Increase Accessibility
ballot_label: Caption: Bonds to Increase Safety, Security; Repair, Construct Schools; Increase Accessibility. Question: Shall District issue bonds, projected to maintain 2026 bond rate, to increase safety, repair, replace aging schools and increase accessibility? If the bonds are approved, they will be payable from taxes on property or property ownership that are not subject to the limits of sections 11 and 11b, Article XI of the Oregon Constitution.
summary: Reynolds School District No. 7 asks to issue $162.5 million in general obligation bonds for capital projects: replacing Glenfair Elementary; districtwide roofing, HVAC, plumbing, electrical and water heater work; fire alarm, PA and perimeter security systems; ADA upgrades; and other projects including a turf field at Reynolds High School. A community oversight committee and regular audits would be required.
yes_means: A yes vote authorizes Reynolds School District to issue $162.5 million in bonds, repaid from property taxes, for safety, security, school repair and replacement, and accessibility projects.
no_means: A no vote does not authorize the district to issue the proposed bonds.
fiscal_impact: Principal of $162.5 million. Projected to maintain the district's 2026 bond levy rate of $1.62 per $1,000 of assessed value, with no increase expected. If passed, the district would receive $8,168,000 in state matching funds through the Oregon School Capital Improvement Match Program.

arguments.author: Reynolds School District (explanatory statement)
arguments.statement: The district's explanatory statement says the bond would replace the 72-year-old Glenfair school, which it describes as overcrowded, containing hazardous materials, and with building and security systems beyond repair.
arguments.excerpt: Replace the 72-year-old school, which is overcrowded, contains hazardous materials, and has building and security systems beyond repair;

arguments.author: Reynolds School District (explanatory statement)
arguments.statement: The explanatory statement says the district would receive $8,168,000 in state matching funds only if the bond passes.
arguments.excerpt: Additionally, the District would receive $8,168,000 in state matching funds through the Oregon School Capital Improvement Match Program, but only if the bond measure passes.

arguments.author: Reynolds School Board (furnished by Michael Reyes, Board Chair)
arguments.statement: The Reynolds School Board argues the measure renews an existing bond and would not be a tax increase, funding repairs, security and the Glenfair Elementary replacement.
arguments.excerpt: we made sure that any ask put before voters would NOT be a tax increase. We’re asking you to renew an existing bond, not approve a new tax.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. M-100)

arguments.author: Reynolds principals (furnished by Joyce Rosenau)
arguments.statement: Reynolds principals argue the bond would fund perimeter fencing, access controls, secure vestibules and door hardware for school security.
arguments.excerpt: Controlling who enters our schools is critical. This bond funds perimeter fencing, new access controls, secure vestibules and door hardware.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. M-100)

arguments.author: Reynolds educators (furnished by Ana Gonzalez Muñoz)
arguments.statement: Reynolds teachers and staff argue the bond problems can be fixed without a rate increase.
arguments.excerpt: The good news? You can fix these problems without raising your taxes. The rate you pay today, you will continue to pay. $0.00 rate increase.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. M-101)

arguments.author: Reynolds taxpayers (furnished by Shelby Tooze-Williams, Margaret Breithaupt and William J. Ohle)
arguments.statement: A taxpayers' argument says the measure would make Reynolds eligible for $8,168,000 in state matching funds that would otherwise go to another district.
arguments.excerpt: This measure also makes Reynolds eligible for $8,168,000 in state matching funds, money that will go to another district if voters don’t renew this bond.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. M-101)
